title: Interstage Synchronizer for Overlap-Aware Kernel Routing and NCCL Stream Prioritization
creator: Amina Patel
description:
Problem statement: On multi-GPU inference rigs we observe suboptimal overlap between compute kernels (attention, matmuls) and inter-GPU communication (NCCL collectives) during the hybrid tensor/pipeline parallel prefill->decode path. This results in wasted device time and tail latency spikes for mid-long sequences. Goal: implement an interstage synchronizer that lets the runtime route kernels and schedule NCCL streams with explicit overlap heuristics so compute and communication can be pipelined across stages without violating KV-cache or ordering constraints.

Scope: implement runtime layer that: (1) collects stage-level metrics (kernel latency histogram, NCCL op duration, stream occupancy); (2) computes per-model routing hints (preferred kernel variant, attention tiling size) for upcoming micro-batches; (3) inserts lightweight interstage barriers that are overlap-friendly (non-blocking handoff) and select NCCL stream priorities for collective ops; (4) integrates with existing kernel selector to prefer attention kernels that expose comm/computation pipelining (e.g., tile-first attention kernel vs fused long-seq kernel) when overlap gains are predicted.

Non-goals: changes to model graph or PT-level rewriter, any new optimizer transforms, or changes to model weights. Not targeting training workloads.

Success metrics: median tail-latency reduction >= 18% on 8xA100 80GB runs for 4k token synthetic traces; 95th percentile latency reduction >= 20% on customer RLHF-ish workload; no regression in throughput for short sequences (<128 tokens).

Design notes and approach:
- Observation: NCCL collectives during prefill tend to bunch up if stages block on large fused kernels. By choosing attention kernels with smaller per-token compute but earlier comm-readiness we can start NCCL earlier and overlap.
- Interstage Synchronizer (ISS) responsibilities:
  * Metric aggregation: sliding-window microsecond histograms for kernel and NCCL ops per stage. Light-weight, in-process.
  * Decision tier: small rule-based policy (first rollout) mapping observed stage metrics + sequence length estimate to kernel_variant_choice, comm_priority_hint, and target micro-batch size. Policy is pluggable; future ML policy planned.
  * Stream control: runtime will create two stream classes per GPU (compute_high and comm_high) and set NCCL ops to comm_high when hint indicates prioritization. Use cudaStreamPriority where available.
  * Handoff primitive: a non-blocking stage-fence that signals downstream stage via event + lightweight token message; avoid cudaDeviceSynchronize-like barriers.
- Kernel selector changes: add an "overlap_score" for each kernel variant computed from historical latency and earliest-comm-emit time; prefer variant with higher overlap_score when policy chooses overlap-first mode.
- Telemetry: expose per-request timeline (kernel start/end, NCCL start/end, event handoff) to Console trace UI for debugging.

Acceptance criteria (must-pass):
1) End-to-end correctness: outputs identical to baseline (bitwise not required but functional parity verified on 1000 samples).
2) Performance: meet success metrics above on benchmark harness.
3) Stability: no increased OOMs or deadlocks across 48-hour soak test at production QPS.
4) Observability: traces for interstage events appear in Console and link to runtimes.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for ISS decision tier (simulated histograms -> expected hints).
- Integration tests on synthetic model (GPT-like) with controlled attention shapes to assert NCCL overlap (measure event interleaving).
- Hardware tests: 4x and 8x A100/MI250 clusters running prefill->decode traces. Compare baseline and feature-on runs.
- Canary rollout: start on dedicated lab cluster with small percentage of production traffic (10%), short window (48h), metric gating.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Choosing smaller attention tiles improves overlap but increases kernel dispatch overhead; need to tune threshold heuristics.
- cudaStreamPriority availability varies by driver/hardware; fallback path needed (use stream ordering + spin-wait heuristics).
- Interaction with KV cache eviction: prefetching ahead of handoff could increase memory pressure—we must gate prefetch by resident memory headroom.

Implementation milestones:
- Week 1: metric aggregation + basic non-blocking handoff primitive (Amina).
- Week 2: kernel selector overlap_score integration + decision tier v0 (Diego).
- Week 3: NCCL stream prioritization and telemetry integration (Diego / infra).
- Week 4: hardware validation and canary rollout; iterate on heuristics (team).

Related artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/l/cp/ISS-design-31207 (internal)
- Benchmark harness: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/benchmarks/iss-multi-gpu (PR forthcoming)
- Console trace prototype: https://console.redwood.ai/traces/issue/ISS-31207

Rollout plan:
1) feature gate disabled by default.
2) Enable on lab clusters for manual runs.
3) Canary on dedicated customers with opt-in.
4) Gradual default enable for runtime-2.4 if metrics stable.
